clue.text: A way through on foot

blocks.note: surface reading: a footpath or passage you walk along
setter's reading: a curved opening you can pass under, which is also the raised part of the sole of your foot

explanation.surface: Directions for a pedestrian route through somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On foot' seems to mean walking, but it locates the thing anatomically: the answer is both a gateway and part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An archway is an opening one passes beneath, and the curved underside of the human sole bears the same name.

clue.text: Extravagantly laud goddess thus?

indicators.note: extravagantly means wildly, beyond normal bounds, so the next word's letters are flung into another order

blocks.note: laud rearranged
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Should one praise a deity over the top in this way?
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is a staple crossword goddess; the whole clue also describes the answer, since worshipping a goddess extravagantly is exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone excessively and fawningly, heaping on flattery, is to adulate them; worship of a goddess fits.

clue.text: Conservative-Labour rift

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the Labour Party sits on the left of British politics

explanation.surface: A political split between Britain's two main parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative and Labour are the two main UK parties, of the right and left respectively.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack or split in rock or a chin is a fissure or division, just as a rift is a gap.

clue.text: Samuel's teacher has a name for writing essays

blocks.note: in the Bible the priest Eli brought up the boy Samuel at Shiloh
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biblical tutor apparently adopting a pen name for his essay-writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb signed his Essays of Elia with this pseudonym; 'has' simply puts the article after the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Elia was the pseudonym Charles Lamb used when publishing his celebrated essays in the London Magazine.

clue.text: In-service instruction

blocks.note: surface reading: on-the-job training for people already employed
setter's reading: a reading from the Bible delivered during a church service, and also a period of teaching

explanation.surface: Professional training given to teachers or staff while working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-service' is jargon for staff training; read as 'in a service' it means in church, where a Bible passage is read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of teaching is a class, and the Bible passage read during church worship has the same name.

clue.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

definitions.text: They should be able to identify any salts in a mixture

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so the two preceding words are blended into one new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chemists who can pick out whatever compounds are present in a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and its last four words are also the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical testers examine samples to determine their composition, which is just what laboratory scientists of this kind do.

clue.text: Family of four girls, followed by three more

definitions.text: Family of four girls, followed by three more

blocks.clueFragment: Family of four girls, followed by three more
blocks.note: surface reading: a household of four daughters that later has three more
setter's reading: the surname of Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy in Little Women is also a month, and the next three months, April, May and June, are girls' names

explanation.surface: A large family growing larger as seven daughters arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Louisa May Alcott's four sisters share the surname; on the calendar the same word is followed by three months that double as girls' names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Women sisters are the Marches, and the calendar's third month precedes April, May and June, all female names.

clue.text: Business studies

blocks.note: surface reading: the academic subject taught at schools and colleges
setter's reading: investigations a company commissions into what customers want

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a school subject, but read literally it means surveys carried out by firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies survey consumers about preferences and buying habits before launching products; such commercial surveys are exactly enquiries done for trade.

clue.text: Total confidence initial odds must be switched? Goodness!

definitions.note: an exclamation in the surface; the definition is the noun meaning virtue

indicators.note: switched means swapped over, so the two named letters trade places

blocks.note: certitude is complete certainty
the odd-numbered letters at the start of that word, its first and third

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at the idea of swapping the odds on a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and third letters of CERTITUDE, C and R, change places; 'Goodness!' looks like an exclamation but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral uprightness and righteousness of conduct amount to virtue, so this word is a formal synonym for moral worth.

clue.text: Premonitions Rigoletto and Richard III had

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing what they possessed; the answer is the plural noun

blocks.note: first meaning: intuitive feelings about what is going to happen
second meaning: Verdi's jester and Shakespeare's king were both humpbacked

explanation.surface: Verdi's jester and Shakespeare's king both sensed doom coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Both characters are traditionally played with a humped back; the word also means intuitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Gut feelings that something will happen are intuitions, and a humped back is likewise called by this plural noun.

clue.text: Break-up of force and loss of rank after accepting false alibis

indicators.note: false means untrue or counterfeit, so the excuse's letters are not in their real order
accepting means taking in, so the word for losing rank holds the rearranged letters inside it

blocks.note: demotion is reduction to a lower rank
alibis rearranged

explanation.surface: An army unit disbanded after a court-martial rejects soldiers' excuses and strips them of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break-up of force' sounds like riot control; it is the standing-down of an army, as after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbanding troops and releasing them from military service at war's end is the standing-down of armed forces.

clue.text: Vain advice to the prodigal

blocks.note: first meaning: futile, of no avail
second meaning, split into two words: a spendthrift should consume a smaller amount

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning breaks the word into two: telling a waster to 'use less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort spent in vain achieves nothing, which is exactly what a futile, pointless thing does.

clue.text: Movie queen from the continent

definitions.note: the queen in the 1951 film The African Queen is a riverboat; the answer is the word naming her

blocks.note: first meaning: the film The ... Queen, starring Bogart and Hepburn, names its boat this kind of queen
second meaning: belonging to or coming from Africa

explanation.surface: A film star of royal standing who comes from mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movie queen' suggests a screen goddess and 'the continent' suggests Europe, as the British use it; neither is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone native to Africa, and completes the title of the Bogart and Hepburn adventure film.

clue.text: A choice literary gathering

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclusive meeting of writers, like a select literary salon
setter's reading: a book that gathers chosen pieces of writing together; the Greek root means a gathering of flowers

explanation.surface: An exclusive party for writers and critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' suggests people meeting, but it is a collection of texts; 'choice' means hand-picked.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a volume collects selected poems or stories by various authors; its Greek origin literally means flower-gathering.

clue.text: Woman who has to polish hard

blocks.note: to polish a text is to revise and improve it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A woman stuck with a tough cleaning job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like housework, but it means revising a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a female first name, and crosswords routinely define any given name as a woman or man.

clue.text: Wit of turbulent priest

indicators.note: something turbulent is churned up and disordered, so the following word's letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric with a stormy temper also has a sharp sense of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word means liveliness of mind and sparkling cleverness, which is what English calls quick humour.

clue.text: Communicate what some crossword answers are

definitions.note: a description of entries, read as past participle

blocks.note: first meaning: to get an idea over to an audience
second meaning: the entries written horizontally in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb means to convey; read literally, horizontal entries are placed left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: To convey an idea successfully is to get it over to listeners, and horizontal grid entries are literally entered that way.

clue.text: They're essential to one's standing as a rider

definitions.text: They're essential to one's standing as a rider

blocks.clueFragment: They're essential to one's standing as a rider
blocks.note: surface reading: things that maintain your reputation or status as a horseman
setter's reading: literally standing up in the saddle, which needs foot supports hanging from it

explanation.surface: What a horseman needs to keep his reputation in the equestrian world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' reads as status; it is literal, rising up on the horse with feet supported.
explanation.definitionFit: These metal loops hang on straps either side of the saddle and hold the rider's feet, letting them stand up.

clue.text: What Cinderella became after twelve

blocks.note: surface reading: at midnight the spell broke and she was a kitchen girl in rags again
setter's reading: twelve as an age, so she turned thirteen

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale heroine's transformation when the clock struck midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' suggests the midnight chimes; it is her age, after which she is in her thirteens to nineteens.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone aged thirteen to nineteen is an adolescent, and every girl becomes one once she passes twelve.

clue.text: Specified limitation of ownership in legal document

indicators.note: something placed in a document sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal instrument, such as a conveyance of property
in English law a fee tail limits who may inherit an estate

explanation.surface: A lawyer describing a precise restriction on property rights written into a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: TAIL, as in entail or fee tail, is a real legal term for restricting who may inherit an estate, so the surface is accurate law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set out item by item, with all particulars given, has been spelt out precisely, so the participle means specified.

clue.text: Edward lifted small firm with spirit and dignity

indicators.note: lifted means raised upward, which in a down entry turns the abbreviation bottom to top

blocks.note: Ed is the short form of Edward
Co. is the abbreviation for company
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Edward makes off with a little business, taking drink and his self-respect along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' looks like stealing; in a down answer it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper, seemly behaviour that respects convention shows composure and propriety, so it matches dignity closely.

clue.text: View a risky venture with trepidation at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: taken as written
spec is short for speculation, a gamble on an uncertain outcome
the initial letter of trepidation

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing a gamble nervously before committing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On spec' means as a speculation, hence a risky venture.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook or prospect, as in a house with a southern aspect, is the scene that can be seen from somewhere.

clue.text: Bar for a daring young high-flier

definitions.text: Bar for a daring young high-flier

blocks.clueFragment: Bar for a daring young high-flier
blocks.note: surface reading: a pub or drinking spot for an ambitious young achiever
setter's reading: the swinging horizontal pole from the old music-hall song about a daring young man who flies through the air, used by circus acrobats

explanation.surface: A trendy watering hole for ambitious young executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub and 'high-flier' a whizz-kid; both are literal, recalling the old music-hall song.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus acrobats swing from a horizontal pole suspended high on two ropes, which is this apparatus.

clue.text: Place of interest it's the custom to be silent going round

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the word for silent surrounds the word for custom

blocks.note: to keep mum is to say nothing
use means habit or custom, as in usage

explanation.surface: A tourist attraction where visitors are expected to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping mum means staying silent; the surface's hushed gallery is apt, but 'place of interest' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A building holding collections for public viewing is a typical attraction that sightseers visit in towns.

clue.text: Come out with me repeatedly to have a drink

indicators.note: out tells us to remove letters, here the word named after with, from the word before it
repeatedly says the trimmed piece is used twice, one copy after the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to step outside, again and again, for a drink together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out with me' reads as an invitation, but it means COME with ME taken out, leaving CO; doubled, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot beverage made from powdered cacao beans mixed with milk or water.

clue.text: Broken rule again leads to suffering

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the words that follow are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking the rules a second time brings pain on the offender.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names intense pain along a nerve, a specific kind of physical affliction the sufferer endures.

clue.text: Spaceman showed open mouthed wonder

blocks.note: the word split off the front of Spaceman: a gap is an empty space
the tail of Spaceman: Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: An astronaut staring in amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaceman' is split into two words: a space, then a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare with the jaw dropped in amazement is to stand agog, with mouth open, which this verb describes.

clue.text: Italian leader to return call about civil disorder

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, in front of all the rest
to return is to go back the way you came, so the little word is read from its end
about means surrounding, so the word for call goes around the other letters

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
the first letter of Italian
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An Italian politician comes back to deal with unrest in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian leader' suggests a prime minister; it only means the first letter of Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds running amok in the streets and fighting authorities are engaged in public violence, which is what civil disorder describes.

clue.text: Bird that's flown approximately East over head

indicators.note: over here means covering on both sides, so the compass bearing wraps around the other word

blocks.note: east-south-east is a compass point a little off due east
a head or headland is a cape jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher noting a bird flying roughly eastwards overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is slang for a prison sentence or prisoner, so a bird that's flown is one who has broken out; 'approximately East' is a near-east bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of jail has flown the coop, and prisoners are jailbirds, so this one has absconded.

clue.text: Builder of a lodge

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who constructs a gatehouse or hunting cabin
setter's reading: a lodge is the local branch of a secretive fraternal society, so the builder is also one of its brethren

explanation.surface: A craftsman putting up a small country house.
explanation.walkthrough: A lodge is the local branch of the Freemasons, so the word fits both a stone builder and a member.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker constructs buildings, and the brotherhood of Freemasons organises its members into local lodges.

clue.text: Play in afternoon, or the other way round

indicators.note: the other way round means facing back to front, so these letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: p.m. stands for post meridiem, after noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Children playing in the afternoon, or perhaps at another time.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic is to play boisterously, running and leaping about in high spirits, as children and animals do.

clue.text: The advantage of keenness

blocks.note: first meaning: a slight lead over a rival, as in having the upper hand
second meaning: sharpness, as of a blade or of a voice

explanation.surface: Praising the benefits of enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keenness' looks like eagerness, but it means sharpness, as a keen blade has.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an edge over competitors means a lead, and a knife's cutting sharpness is also called its edge.
